title: EMMA plugin manifest
description: Identity, trust and resource limits for one plugin. Everything about what the plugin serves (kinds, filters, sorts, settings) comes from meta.describe() at run time, so it cannot drift from the code. The manifest is the signed part: the host reads it before it executes any plugin code. A package is a zip holding exactly plugin.json and the one entrypoint file named below; any other file is refused. See docs/architecture/plugin-trust.md.

schema.description: Manifest format version. Hosts refuse versions they do not know.

id.description: Stable plugin identifier: lower-case reverse-DNS style. The host namespaces every node by this id, so it must never change once published.

kinds.description: Display-only summary of the kinds the plugin serves, for repository listings that must not load the plugin. The host validates it against meta.describe() when the plugin is installed and again on load, and refuses a mismatch.

icon.description: How the plugin's own icon is presented. Carried over from the old manifest's thumbnail block.

contract.description: The WIT interfaces the component implements, by interface id. The host checks these against the component's real exports; the exports are authoritative.

required.description: Interfaces the plugin cannot run without. The base world only.

optional.description: Extension interfaces the plugin implements, such as emma:core/search-assist@1.

transport.description: How the host runs the plugin. Only wasm exists today. 'process' is reserved for the deferred out-of-process mode and must be rejected until it is implemented.

entrypoint.description: The component file inside the package, and its digest. The digest is mandatory so the signature covers the code, not just the manifest.

path.description: Relative path, no '..' segments, no leading slash, ends in .wasm or .cwasm. Compared by path-segment, never by string prefix.

permissions.description: What the plugin may ask the host for. Anything not listed is denied. There is deliberately no filesystem permission: a Wasm plugin has no filesystem.

network.description: Exact host names (lower-case) or '*.example.com' wildcards the plugin may fetch. Empty means no network.

limits.description: Resource ceilings enforced by the Wasm runtime.

signature.description: Repository signature over the manifest. Required by any host that enforces signatures (the default); absent only for unsigned local development installs, on hosts configured to allow them. A signature that is present must always verify. The signed bytes are length-prefixed binary frames, not JSON text.

repositoryId.description: Must equal the repository the package came from as known to the host. The host never uses this value to locate files.

manifestSha256.description: Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the manifest digest: the parsed fields in a fixed order through length-prefixed framing, signature excluded (ManifestDigest). Not a hash of the JSON text, so whitespace and key order are irrelevant.

interfaceId.description: A WIT interface id with its major version, e.g. emma:core/catalog@1.

identifier.description: 1 to 128 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit. Contains no path separator, so it can never name a file outside the directory it is joined to.
